property_summary: For any non-empty _tos and any amount v and source address, calling C.transfer(...) returns true (completes successfully) and the successful completion is independent of incrementing the amount passed to the external transferFrom; the mutant that passes v+1 can cause a different observable outcome (failure/false) for some inputs when the callee enforces exact amount, so the reference always returns true while the mutant can fail for some inputs.

For any inputs where _tos is non-empty and the callee contract's transferFrom call succeeds, the reference contract's transfer returns (does not revert) while the mutant inverts the success check and will revert when the callee call succeeds—so the reference never reverts for a successful downstream call but the mutant can.

For any non-empty _tos array and any callee contract, C.transfer either completes successfully only if every low-level transferFrom call to the callee succeeds; the mutant that ignores call return values can return true even when a callee call fails — therefore the reference always reverts when any sub-call reverts, while the mutant may not.

For any callee address that implements transferFrom(address,address,uint256) but does NOT implement transfer(address,address,uint256), calling C.transfer(...) always succeeds (reference calls transferFrom), whereas the mutant that calls transfer(...) will fail when the callee lacks transfer(address,address,uint256).
